objective: Using YAM and a full-scale turning peel, rotate a roughly 300 mm partially baked pizza approximately 180 degrees about its initial center inside a representative closed-roof 16-inch pizza oven. Preserve crust-to-stone support and a maximum 50 mm center excursion throughout; leave the pizza top-side-up and fully contained; release it stably and withdraw the peel. This tests confined blade insertion and repeated low-lift tangential traction, not cooking chemistry.
instruction: Turn the pizza approximately 180 degrees using the turning peel. Keep its crust supported by the oven deck and its center within 50 mm of its starting position throughout. Leave it top-side-up inside the oven, release it stably, and fully withdraw the peel. Any physically safe stroke count, arm choice, regrasp, or action order is allowed.
industrial_mapping: Impact on jobs: in-oven pizza turning is food-preparation work performed by pizza and restaurant cooks. Manufacturer instructions describe sliding a peel beneath the pizza, rotating it in the oven, and maintaining baking-stone contact. The tested ability is steering a long tool beneath a weakly constrained food item and producing centered rotation under roof and mouth constraints while preserving deck support. This differs from generic rigid-object rotation, pizza launching, or appearance recognition.
damage_rules: At reset define disjoint collider-owner sets C=pizza core and articulated rim, T=separable toppings, D=cordierite deck, L=complete peel, L_tip=nonempty authored leading-edge peel colliders, G=YAM fingers and palms, R=other YAM colliders, Q=G union R, and O=oven roof, lintel, walls, burner guard, and shell. T is not part of C, and T-D contact is not crust support.

At every physics substep k, sample after integration and contact resolution: transforms, velocities, joints, resolved manifolds, nonnegative normal impulses Jn in N·s, and signed collider-surface separations d in metres. F_AB(k)=sum(Jn for all A-B points)/dt, with dt=1/240 s natively and 1/480 s in refinement. Positive d is clearance, zero is touching, and negative d is penetration.

For every named global signed-separation metric, enumerate every collision-shape pair in the named owner sets and compute S_AB=min over all scored substeps and pairs d_ab(k). Empty required sets are configuration failures. Signed deck separation uses the same definition. Positive deck gap is g_CD(k)=min over C-D pairs max(d_cd(k),0), reduced as G_CD=max_k g_CD(k); it is distinct from SUPPORT and normal load F_CD.

An A-B contact event is a maximal consecutive sequence of post-resolution samples containing resolved A-B contact. Event impulse is the sum of Jn across all event points and samples; peak force is max F_AB(k). One contact-free physics sample closes the event. Counters and latches initialize only at native reset.

CRUST_PUNCTURE latches if S_LC<-0.003 m, F_LC(k)>40 N for six consecutive native samples, or an L_tip collider crosses from wholly above the core top to intersecting or below the core underside between adjacent samples without resolved endpoint contact or a CCD hit. The force counter resets on absent contact or F_LC<=40 N. Six native samples and twelve refinement samples both represent 0.025 s.

PERMANENT_RIM_FOLD latches if a rim joint exceeds 12 degrees or 0.008 m from neutral and, after all L-C contact ends, remains beyond 8 degrees or 0.005 m for 240 consecutive native samples. Its residual counter resets when both residuals return within bounds or L-C contact resumes.

For topping t, DETACHED_t(k) means no resolved t-C contact after resolution. Its counter increments on consecutive detached samples and resets when contact returns. TOPPING_LOSS latches at 60 consecutive native samples, or 0.25 s. A 1-59-sample separation is tolerated solely as contact jitter; 60 samples fails even if the topping remains over C or rests on D.
OVERTURN latches when the core top normal has world-z component below zero. UPRIGHT requires n_z>=cos(30 degrees)=0.866 at every scored sample; any violation permanently revokes eligibility.

COLLISION_DAMAGE latches when any L-O or Q-O event has peak force greater than 100 N or accumulated normal impulse greater than 5 N·s. These provisional conservative limits include the entire peel and every robot link.
DIRECT_GRIPPER_BYPASS latches on any resolved G-C or G-T contact. G-L contact for grasping or regrasping the peel is allowed.

Represent the oven interior with reset-fixed inward half-spaces, including its mouth plane. At every native sample transform all C and T collision shapes into the oven frame. Use deterministic support queries for convex shapes and every transformed collision vertex for triangle meshes. CONTAINED holds only when every half-space margin is nonnegative; the first negative margin latches OUTSIDE_OVEN.

SUPPORT holds only when at least one resolved C-D manifold exists. One native sample without one latches SUPPORT_LOSS. T-D, L-C, and L-D cannot substitute. CENTER_LIMIT_BREACH latches when norm(c_xy-c0_xy)>0.050 m.

INACCESSIBLE_LOSS latches if the core center is over 0.050 m below the deck top, any C or T collider exits an oven wall or mouth, or C enters the reset-fixed outside-workcell catch volume. IK failure alone is not loss.

Any post-reset C or T pose/velocity write, task-object weld, hidden pivot, post-reset collision filtering, disabled collision or gravity, or scorer-state mutation is INVALID_SHORTCUT and forces zero. Slip, folding, puncture, topping loss, support loss, collision, and falling must remain physically possible.

For refinement, E_LC is the native L-C event with greatest peak force, ties earliest. Its matched half-open window begins at the 20 Hz boundary at or before its first sample and ends at the first boundary after its last sample. At 480 Hz select the L-C event beginning in that window with greatest peak force, ties earliest. Relative difference is abs(P480-P240)/max(abs(P240),1 N). No contact in either replay gives zero; contact in exactly one gives positive infinity.

All scoring predicates use fresh post-resolution observations. Reversible counters reset exactly as defined; irreversible latches persist until reset. Scores, journals, screenshots, and video from other native trial IDs are excluded.
assets: Pinned YAM embodiment and native gripper controls from yam-isaac-lab-arena commit 0059d02a1a91bc6834c1d0846022891df0c78730, IsaacLab-Arena commit c7edf3a9d5d8276565208f72422f8f8a0806d6cf, and Isaac Sim 6.1.0.0; pinned API and AssetRegistry compatibility remain an unverified construction gate.
Independently authored representative closed-roof oven preserving the documented 630 x 580 x 370 mm exterior, 16-inch capacity, and 15 mm cordierite deck.
Full-scale turning peel preserving the documented 170 x 800 x 20 mm envelope and 0.4 kg mass.
Approximately 300 mm pizza with rigid set underside/core, shallow collision-enabled articulated rim, core-fixed asymmetric yaw marker, and separable rigid toppings.
Fixed external and wrist RGB-D cameras using the common observation structure.
Collision-enabled workcell geometry exposing handle, mouth, roof, robot-link, fall, and withdrawal-clearance failures.
approximations: Cooking, heat transfer, changing browning, smoke, thermal hazards, and food safety are excluded. Fixed browning asymmetry is only a yaw marker.
The pizza uses rigid PhysX bodies and a shallow articulated rim solely for blade-entry compliance; it makes no raw-dough or general deformable-food claim.

Only oven exterior size, capacity, stone thickness, and peel size and mass are documented measurements. Pizza mass, interior mouth and roof geometry, blade bevel, friction, restitution, rim properties, force limits, penetration tolerances, and camera thresholds are explicit provisional engineering assumptions requiring native calibration.

Initial stability is a hands-off 240-native-sample settle. Drift extrema reference its first sample; terminal speed, initial contacts, yaw, and untouched score use its last sample. Trajectory checks cover every later native sample through termination.
Joint margin is min(q-q_lower,q_upper-q). Tracking error is abs(q_command-q) at 20 Hz boundaries, with commands held between boundaries. Joint speed is abs(delta q/dt) at physics rate.

During samples with peel centre-of-mass speed greater than 0.010 m/s, group G-L manifolds by finger link. An opposed pair requires positive-impulse patches on matching left and right fingers whose L-directed normals have dot product<=-0.5. Reduce disjoint pair count by the minimum over active samples; peel motion without a qualifying active sample fails configuration.

Cameras render once only after each fully completed 20 Hz control interval. Let m be the number of complete control intervals before termination and n=m. A terminal physics sample occurring inside an interval produces no extra frame; termination at that interval's final substep produces its normal frame. Both cameras must have exactly n indexed frames. Missing indexed frames are invalid, and n=0 fails every camera check.

An RGB frame is valid only when all pixels are finite, it is nonconstant, and maximum channelwise range is at least 5/255. RGB validity is valid frames/n per camera, reduced by the worst camera. Depth validity v_jf is the fraction of pixels finite and strictly between configured near and far planes; missing or zero-pixel frames contribute zero, reduced by the worst frame and camera.

Segmentation ownership is C union T for pizza and L for peel. A target-visible frame has at least 1% pizza-owned pixels and 1% peel-owned pixels. Visibility is qualifying frames/n per camera, reduced by the worst camera.

Refinement replays the identical seed, reset, materials, 20 Hz timestamped action journal, and native horizon at 480 Hz. Its duration ends at the first 20 Hz boundary at or after native termination. Refinement validates physics only and cannot change the native grade.

Local component tests produced about 175-179 degrees rotation and 27-33 mm excursion across nominal, friction, compliance, and half-timestep conditions. They are prototype evidence, not native YAM certification. Full-scale physical grasp, reach, roof and handle clearance, insertion, traction, joint/body traces, release, and withdrawal remain mandatory unverified gates.
scoring_spec: Let native step 0 be the final hands-off settle sample; freeze core center c0 and marker yaw yaw0. For every later 240 Hz post-resolution sample k, e_k=norm(c_xy(k)-c0_xy), E_k=max_{0<=j<=k}e_j, wrap180(a)=((a+180 deg) mod 360 deg)-180 deg, and Y_k=abs(wrap180(yaw(k)-yaw0)). SUPPORT_ALL, CONTAINED_ALL, and UPRIGHT_ALL require their predicates at every sample through k. RELEASED(k) holds iff no L-C, L-T, G-C, or G-T contact exists, core linear speed<=0.02 m/s, and core angular speed<=5 deg/s. WITHDRAWN(k) holds iff every L shape is wholly outside on the mouth side, each shape's maximum inward mouth-plane margin<=0, and min signed separation between L and C union T is>=0.050 m. SAFE(k) requires the three ALL predicates, E_k<=0.050 m, and absence of every damage or shortcut latch. Eligibility counter r starts at zero, increments only while RELEASED, WITHDRAWN, and SAFE are simultaneously true, and otherwise resets. ELIGIBLE first becomes true at 240 fresh consecutive native samples. At that first eligible sample score=1.0 if 150<=Y_k<=180 degrees, score=0.5 if 90<=Y_k<150 degrees, otherwise score=0. No bonus exists. Record terminal observations and stop commands and physics immediately. If eligibility never occurs by native step 28800, score=0. Before termination the displayed score is provisional zero. A hard-failure latch irrevocably forces zero and revokes prior dwell progress. Stroke count, hand identity, action count, regrasp strategy, peel-contact pattern, and order do not affect grading. Untouched release and withdrawal score zero because Y<90 degrees. Directed rotation beyond 180 degrees is graded by wrapped yaw, so 210 degrees maps to 150 degrees. The 20 Hz journal records commanded and measured joints and grippers; the 240 Hz journal records every defined observable, counter, event, and latch in sampling order. Only the current native trial ID may supply evidence or score.
